messages.subject: MLR scaling correction factor = NA
parts:
Hi everyone, 

I am running a simple interaction model with all continuous observed variables. Most of my variables are non-normal and I have some missing data, so I am using the MLR estimator with missing = 'fiml'. My model converges and prints an output, however, the scaling correction factor under the Robust column is NA. Can anyone advise me as to why this might be happening. 

Here is my model:

Mod1.3 <- 

  'SA10 ~ IQ.all + SES.all + SA7 + SCDiff7 + Friend.all + SCDiff7:Friend.all'

Fit1.3 <- sem(Mod1.3, data = FD2, estimator = "MLR", missing = "fiml") 

I would really appreciate any advice!

Best,
Hannah

messages.subject: Re: MLR scaling correction factor = NA
parts: Can anyone advise me as to why this might be happening.

Your model has df = 0, so a scaling factor is irrelevant in this case.  Do you get a scaling factor if you add any constraints? (e.g., SA10 ~ 0*1 constrains the intercept to zero, which I'm sure you do not want to do, but it is just an example).

messages.subject: Re: MLR scaling correction factor = NA
parts: Mod1.2 is not converging and I cannot understand why

Neither can I.  I ran lavaanify() on your syntaxes (syntaces?) and the parameter tables appear as expected.  Does this (equivalent) model converge?

'SA10 ~ IQ.all + SES.all + SA7 + SCDiff7 + Friend.all'

If so, it might be necessary to post your data for Yves to track down the problem.

FYI, since these are ordinary regression models, lavaan actually just reverts to OLS estimation behind the scenes.  So other than the perks of using lavaan (e.g., easy to get a standardized solution), you could just use the lm() function, or the glm() function if you want to use MLE. 

OLSmod1.2 <- lm(SA10 ~ IQ.all + SES.all + SA7 + SCDiff7 + Friend.all, data = FD2)
OLSmod1.3 <- lm(SA10 ~ IQ.all + SES.all + SA7 + SCDiff7 + Friend.all + Friend.all:SCDiff7, data = FD2)
anova(OLSmod1.2, OLSmod1.3, test = "F")
summary(OLSmod1.3)
confint(OLSmod1.3)
## for standardized slopes:
coef(lm(SA10 ~ scale(IQ.all) + scale(SES.all) + scale(SA7) + scale(SCDiff7) * scale(Friend.all), data = FD2))

or using MLE:

MLEmod1.2 <- glm(SA10 ~ IQ.all + SES.all + SA7 + SCDiff7 + Friend.all, data = FD2)
MLEmod1.3 <- glm(SA10 ~ IQ.all + SES.all + SA7 + SCDiff7 + Friend.all + Friend.all:SCDiff7, data = FD2)
anova(MLEmod1.2, MLEmod1.3, test = "LRT")
summary(MLEmod1.3)
confint(MLEmod1.3)

messages.subject: Re: MLR scaling correction factor = NA
parts: Do you have any idea why this might be/ why the statement missing = "fiml" may be stopping the model from converging?

No, it would probably be necessary to see your data.  Since you have missing data, leaving that option out means using listwise deletion, so the model is converging on a smaller subsample of your data.
otherwise I am performing the analyses on a more restricted sample if I use glm()?

Right, I forgot about the missing data.  The lm() or glm() option would be viable if you use multiple imputation, though.  The Amelia package has a convenient mi.meld() function for pooling estimates and SEs, although calculating a model-comparison test would be a little more complicated.  I have some syntax I teach with that you could use, if you can't get the FIML issue sorted out.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: MLR scaling correction factor = NA
parts:
Is there anyway to prevent my model (below) from going back to using OLS estimation and instead use ML estimation?

Mod1.3 <- 'SA10 ~ IQ.all + SES.all + SA7 + SCDiff7 + Friend.all + Friend.all:SCDiff7'

You can use Wald chi-squared tests by fitting the full model with each parameter (that you intend to test) labeled.  You then test 1 or more effects equaling zero by specifying those constraints in the lavTestWald() function.  Because the interaction term apparently MUST remain in your model for it to converge, you can test lower-order effects by fixing both it/they and the interaction effect to zero.  For example:

mod.full <- ' x9 ~ b1*x1 + b2*x2 + b3*x3 + b23*x2:x3 '
fit.full <- sem(mod.full, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, estimator = "MLR")
summary(fit.full)

lavTestWald(fit.full, constraints = 'b1 == 0') # test effect of x1
lavTestWald(fit.full, constraints = 'b23 == 0') # test interaction effect

# simultaneously test interaction effect and one lower-order effect
lavTestWald(fit.full, constraints = 'b23 == 0 ; b2 == 0')
# simultaneously test interaction effect and the other lower-order effect
lavTestWald(fit.full, constraints = 'b23 == 0 ; b3 == 0')
# simultaneously test interaction effect and both lower-order effects
lavTestWald(fit.full, constraints = 'b23 == 0 ; b2 == 0 ; b3 == 0')

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: MLR scaling correction factor = NA
parts: I would just like to clarify if my red model above is using the MLR estimation and providing me with robust estimates

It is using robust ML.  From what I understand, lavaan just uses OLS to find ML estimates in the simple case of unconstrained univariate linear regression with fixed.x = TRUE and complete data; in other words, a situation where you could use lm().  As soon as you request FIML, fixed.x = FALSE, constrained parameters, or a robust estimator, it will not use OLS to find ML estimates.  In the very simple case, OLS estimates are ML estimates, but OLS just finds ML estimates in a single step rather than iteratively, but everything can still be interpreted as ML results.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
